docs.title: Document Classification and Information Extraction System
Overview
docs.text: This project implements an end-to-end system for document classification and information extraction, specifically designed for processing invoices and other business documents. The system combines OCR, machine learning, and NLP techniques to automatically classify documents and extract key information fields.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Document Classification: Support for multiple ML models (SVM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, LSTM, Transformer)
  • Information Extraction: Field-specific extraction using regex and NLP techniques
  • OCR Integration: Robust text extraction from scanned documents
  • REST API: Flask-based API for easy integration
  • Web Interface: User-friendly interface for document upload and processing

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The document processing system exposes a REST API for document classification and information extraction. The API is built using Flask and provides endpoints for single document processing, batch processing, and model management.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: http://localhost:5002/api/v1

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API endpoints require authentication using a JWT token:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" http://localhost:5002/api/v1/...

docs.title: Classify Single Document
docs.text:
POST /classify

Request Body: 

{
    "document": {
        "text": "Document text content",
        "metadata": {
            "source": "file_upload",
            "filename": "document.pdf"
        }
    }
}

Response: 

{
    "status": "success",
    "result": {
        "category": "invoice",
        "confidence": 0.95,
        "processing_time": 0.25
    }
}

docs.title: Python Client Example

from document_processor_client import DocumentProcessorClient

# Initialize client
client = DocumentProcessorClient(
    base_url="http://localhost:5002/api/v1",
    api_key="your_api_key"
)

# Classify document
result = client.classify_document(
    text="Document text content",
    metadata={"filename": "document.pdf"}
)

# Extract fields
fields = client.extract_fields(
    text="Document text content",
    category="invoice",
    metadata={"filename": "document.pdf"}
)

# Batch processing
batch_results = client.process_batch([
    {"text": "Doc 1", "category": "invoice"},
    {"text": "Doc 2", "category": "receipt"}
])

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
The document processing system follows a modular architecture with distinct components for each stage of the pipeline:

graph TD
    A[Document Input] --> B[Preprocessing]
    B --> C[OCR Processing]
    C --> D[Text Classification]
    D --> E[Information Extraction]
    E --> F[Output Generation]

docs.title: 1. Preprocessing Module
docs.text:
Located in src/preprocessing/, this module handles: - Document format conversion (PDF to images) - Image preprocessing (deskewing, noise removal) - Label hint removal for training data - Text normalization

Key classes: - DocumentPreprocessor: Main preprocessing pipeline - ImageProcessor: Image-specific operations - TextNormalizer: Text cleaning and normalization

docs.title: 2. OCR Module
docs.text:
Located in src/ocr/, this module: - Integrates with Tesseract OCR - Handles multi-page documents - Performs OCR quality assessment - Extracts text with confidence scores

Key classes: - OCREngine: Main OCR processing - OCRQualityAssessor: Quality metrics - MultiPageProcessor: Handles multi-page documents

docs.title: 3. Classification Module
docs.text:
Located in src/classification/, this module: - Implements multiple classifier models - Handles feature extraction - Manages model training and evaluation - Provides model comparison utilities

Key classes: - EnhancedDocumentClassifier: Main classifier implementation - ClassifierComparison: Model comparison and evaluation - FeatureExtractor: Feature generation

docs.title: 4. Extraction Module
docs.text:
Located in src/extraction/, this module: - Implements field-specific extraction rules - Uses regex and NLP for information extraction - Handles validation and post-processing - Manages extraction templates

Key classes: - FieldExtractor: Field-specific extraction - ExtractionManager: Extraction pipeline - ValidationEngine: Result validation

docs.title: 5. Evaluation Module
docs.text:
Located in src/evaluation/, this module: - Implements evaluation metrics - Generates confusion matrices - Performs cross-validation - Handles model comparison

Key classes: - ModelEvaluator: Main evaluation pipeline - MetricsCalculator: Performance metrics - ConfusionMatrixGenerator: Visualization

• Uses TF-IDF features
  • Linear and RBF kernels

svm_model = SVC(
    kernel='linear',
    C=1.0,
    probability=True
)

• Handles sequential text data

class LSTMModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embedding_dim, hidden_dim, output_dim):

        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(embedding_dim, hidden_dim, batch_first=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)

docs.title: 1. Data Preparation
docs.text:
def prepare_training_data(texts, labels):
    # Split data
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        texts, labels,
        test_size=0.2,
        stratify=labels,
        random_state=42
    )

    # Vectorize text
    X_train_vec = vectorizer.fit_transform(X_train)
    X_test_vec = vectorizer.transform(X_test)

    return X_train_vec, X_test_vec, y_train, y_test

docs.title: 2. Model Training
docs.text:
def train_model(model, X_train, y_train):
    # Cross-validation
    cv_scores = cross_val_score(
        model, X_train, y_train,
        cv=5, scoring='f1_weighted'
    )

    # Final training
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)

    return model, cv_scores

def plot_confusion_matrix(cm, classes):
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
    sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues')
    plt.title('Confusion Matrix')
    plt.ylabel('True Label')
    plt.xlabel('Predicted Label')
    plt.xticks(ticks=range(len(classes)), labels=classes, rotation=45)
    plt.yticks(ticks=range(len(classes)), labels=classes, rotation=0)

docs.title: Model Selection
docs.text:
The system uses a combination of metrics to select the best model:

Primary Metrics

  • F1 Score (weighted)

  • Accuracy

  • Training Time

Secondary Metrics

  • Memory Usage

  • Inference Speed

  • Model Size

def select_best_model(results):
    best_model = None
    best_score = -1

    for model_name, metrics in results.items():
        score = (
            0.6 * metrics['f1'] +
            0.2 * metrics['accuracy'] -
            0.2 * metrics['training_time']
        )

        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best_model = model_name

    return best_model

# Main processing pipeline in main.py
class DocumentProcessor:
    def process_document(self, file_path: str, category: str):
        # 1. Preprocessing
        preprocessed = self.preprocessor.process(file_path)

        # 2. OCR Processing
        ocr_results = self.ocr_processor.extract_text(preprocessed)

        # 3. Field Extraction
        extracted_fields = self.extractor.extract_fields(
            ocr_results['text'],
            ocr_results['boxes'],
            category
        )

        # 4. Validation and Post-processing
        validated_fields = self.validator.validate(extracted_fields)

        return validated_fields

docs.text: The dataset management system handles the preparation, augmentation, and validation of training data for both classification and extraction tasks. It includes tools for generating synthetic documents and managing real-world document collections.

docs.title: 1. Document Collection
docs.text:
class DocumentCollector:
    def __init__(self, source_dirs):
        self.source_dirs = source_dirs

    def collect_documents(self):
        documents = []
        for source_dir in self.source_dirs:
            for file_path in Path(source_dir).glob('**/*.pdf'):
                documents.append({
                    'path': str(file_path),
                    'type': self._infer_type(file_path),
                    'metadata': self._extract_metadata(file_path)
                })
        return documents

docs.title: 2. Label Management
docs.text:
class LabelManager:
    def __init__(self, label_map):
        self.label_map = label_map

    def assign_labels(self, documents):
        labeled_docs = []
        for doc in documents:
            label = self._determine_label(doc)
            labeled_docs.append({
                **doc,
                'label': label,
                'label_id': self.label_map[label]
            })
        return labeled_docs

docs.title: 3. Data Splitting
docs.text:
def split_dataset(documents, test_size=0.2, val_size=0.1):
    # Stratified split to maintain class distribution
    train_docs, test_docs = train_test_split(
        documents,
        test_size=test_size,
        stratify=[doc['label'] for doc in documents],
        random_state=42
    )

    train_docs, val_docs = train_test_split(
        train_docs,
        test_size=val_size/(1-test_size),
        stratify=[doc['label'] for doc in train_docs],
        random_state=42
    )

    return train_docs, val_docs, test_docs

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
class AugmentationPipeline:
    def __init__(self, templates, augmentor):
        self.templates = templates
        self.augmentor = augmentor

    def generate_synthetic(self, original_doc, num_copies=5):
        synthetic_docs = []
        for _ in range(num_copies):
            # Generate fields
            fields = self._generate_fields(original_doc)

            # Generate text
            text = self._generate_text(fields)

            # Generate layout
            layout = self._generate_layout(text)

            # Apply augmentation
            augmented = self.augmentor.augment(layout)

            synthetic_docs.append({
                'text': text,
                'image': augmented,
                'fields': fields,
                'label': original_doc['label']
            })

        return synthetic_docs

class DataValidator:

                errors.append(rule.error_message)
        return errors

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The information extraction system is designed to extract structured information from documents after classification. Our implementation focuses on two main approaches: 1. Enhanced Rule-Based Extraction 2. CUTIE (Convolutional Universal Text Information Extractor)

docs.title: Extraction Pipeline
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Classified Document] --> B[OCR Text Extraction]
    B --> C[Text Preprocessing]
    C --> D[Field Extraction]
    D --> E[Post-processing]
    E --> F[Validation]
    F --> G[Structured Output]

docs.title: 1. Enhanced Rule-Based Extraction
docs.text:
The enhanced extractor combines regex patterns, positional analysis, and contextual rules to extract information:

class EnhancedFieldExtractor:
    def extract_fields(self, text: str, boxes: List[Dict[str, int]], doc_type: str):
        # 1. Apply text normalization
        normalized_text = self.text_analyzer.normalize_text(text)

        # 2. Use regex patterns with context
        regex_results = self._extract_with_regex(normalized_text, doc_type)

        # 3. Apply positional analysis
        positional_results = self._extract_with_position(text, boxes)

        # 4. Combine results with confidence scoring
        return self._merge_results(regex_results, positional_results)

Key features of the enhanced extractor: - Advanced text normalization - Context-aware pattern matching - Position-based field identification - Confidence scoring for extracted values

docs.title: 2. CUTIE Implementation
docs.text:
We use CUTIE for handling complex document layouts and field extraction:

class CUTIEExtractor:
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = self._load_model()
        self.tokenizer = self._initialize_tokenizer()

    def extract(self, document):
        # 1. Convert document to grid representation
        grid = self._create_grid(document)

        # 2. Apply CUTIE model
        predictions = self.model.predict(grid)

        # 3. Post-process results
        return self._process_predictions(predictions)

CUTIE advantages: - Grid-based document representation - Better handling of spatial relationships - Improved accuracy for structured documents - Learning from visual layouts

docs.title: 1. Key-Value Fields
docs.text:
Examples: Invoice numbers, dates, amounts 

def extract_key_value(text: str, key: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    patterns = {
        'invoice_number': r'(?i)invoice\s*(?:#|number|num|no)[\.:]?\s*([A-Za-z0-9\-]+)',
        'date': r'(?i)date[\.:]?\s*(\d{1,2}[-/\.]\d{1,2}[-/\.]\d{2,4})',
        'amount': r'(?i)total[\.:]?\s*(?:[\$\£\€])?\s*(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})?)'
    }

    match = re.search(patterns[key], text)
    if match:
        return {
            'value': match.group(1),
            'confidence': 0.9,
            'method': 'regex'
        }
    return None

docs.title: 2. Tabular Data
docs.text:
Example: Line items, product details 

def extract_table_data(text: str, boxes: List[Dict[str, int]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    # 1. Identify table region
    table_region = find_table_region(boxes)

    # 2. Extract rows and columns
    rows = extract_table_rows(text, table_region)

    # 3. Structure the data
    return [
        {
            'description': row['text'],
            'quantity': row['quantity'],
            'price': row['price'],
            'total': row['total']
        }
        for row in rows
    ]

docs.title: 1. Field Validation
docs.text:
def validate_field(field: str, value: Any) -> bool:
    validators = {
        'invoice_number': lambda x: bool(re.match(r'^[A-Za-z0-9\-]{4,}$', x)),
        'date': lambda x: bool(dateparser.parse(x)),
        'amount': lambda x: bool(re.match(r'^\d+(\.\d{2})?$', x.replace(',', '')))
    }

    return validators.get(field, lambda x: True)(value)

docs.title: 2. Confidence Scoring
docs.text:
def calculate_confidence(extraction_result: Dict[str, Any]) -> float:
    factors = {
        'pattern_match': 0.4,
        'position_score': 0.3,
        'validation_score': 0.3
    }

    return sum(
        score * factors[factor]
        for factor, score in extraction_result['scores'].items()
    )

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text: The document processing system is designed with a modular architecture that enables flexible processing of various document types. The system follows a clear pipeline structure where each module handles a specific task and passes its output to the next module.

docs.title: 1. Document Input Module
docs.text: Located in src/uploaded_files/ - Handles document uploads - Supports multiple formats (PDF, images) - Validates input files - Manages file storage

docs.title: 2. Preprocessing Module
docs.text: Located in src/preprocessing/ - Converts PDFs to images (300-600 DPI) - Applies image enhancements: - Grayscale conversion - Noise removal - CLAHE contrast enhancement - Adaptive thresholding - Skew correction - Outputs enhanced images for OCR

docs.title: 3. OCR Module
docs.text: Located in src/ocr/ - Uses pytesseract (OEM 1, PSM 6 & 11) - Extracts text and bounding boxes - Supports multilingual OCR - Provides confidence scores - Outputs structured text data

docs.title: 4. Classification Module
docs.text: Located in src/classification/ - Implements multiple models: - SVM - Random Forest - Logistic Regression - Gradient Boosting - LSTM - Transformers - Uses features: - TF-IDF - Document length - Layout features - Outputs document category

docs.title: 5. Extraction Module
docs.text: Located in src/extraction/ - Traditional methods: - Regex for dates, totals, IDs - spaCy NER for entities - Positional heuristics - Advanced models: - BiLSTM-CRF - LayoutLM - CUTIE - GCN - Extracts 20+ fields with confidence scores

docs.title: 6. Output Module
docs.text: Located in src/processed_files/ - Formats results as JSON/CSV - Includes confidence scores - Maintains audit trail - Supports batch processing

    A[Document Upload] --> B[Preprocessing]

docs.title: 1. Input to Preprocessing
docs.text:
def process_uploaded_file(file_path):
    # Validate file
    if not validate_file(file_path):
        raise ValueError("Invalid file format")

    # Convert to image
    images = pdf_to_images(file_path)

    # Enhance images
    enhanced_images = enhance_images(images)

    return enhanced_images

docs.title: 2. Preprocessing to OCR
docs.text:
def perform_ocr(enhanced_images):
    # Initialize OCR engine
    ocr_engine = OCREngine()

    # Process each page
    results = []
    for image in enhanced_images:
        text, boxes = ocr_engine.process(image)
        results.append({
            'text': text,
            'boxes': boxes,
            'confidence': ocr_engine.get_confidence()
        })

    return results

docs.title: 3. OCR to Classification
docs.text:
def classify_document(ocr_results):
    # Extract features
    features = extract_features(ocr_results)

    # Load classifier
    classifier = load_classifier()

    # Predict category
    category = classifier.predict(features)
    confidence = classifier.predict_proba(features)

    return category, confidence

docs.title: 4. Classification to Extraction
docs.text:
def extract_information(ocr_results, category):
    if category != 'invoice':
        return None

    # Initialize extractor
    extractor = FieldExtractor()

    # Extract fields
    fields = extractor.extract(ocr_results)

    return fields

docs.title: Performance Monitoring
docs.text:
Each module tracks: - Processing time - Success rate - Error rate - Resource usage

class ModuleMetrics:
    def __init__(self, module_name):
        self.module_name = module_name
        self.metrics = {
            'processing_time': [],
            'success_rate': 0,
            'error_rate': 0,
            'resource_usage': {}
        }

    def update_metrics(self, processing_time, success, error, resources):
        self.metrics['processing_time'].append(processing_time)
        if success:
            self.metrics['success_rate'] += 1
        if error:
            self.metrics['error_rate'] += 1
        self.metrics['resource_usage'].update(resources)

docs.title: Project Setup
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone https://github.com/Wisammad/InovoiceScanner.git
cd InovoiceScanner

  2. Create and activate a virtual environment: 

    python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

  3. Install dependencies: 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  4. Set up the project structure: 

    # Create necessary directories
mkdir -p data/raw/{Invoices,PurchaseOrders,Monthly,MonthlyCategory,Shipping orders}
mkdir -p data/processed/{images,text,metadata}
mkdir -p data/models/{classification,extraction}
mkdir -p src/uploaded_files

docs.text:
# Start the main processing pipeline
python src/main.py

This will: - Initialize all components - Start the document processor - Begin monitoring for new documents

docs.title: 2. Start the API Server
docs.text:
# Start the API server (in a new terminal)
python src/api.py

The API server will be available at: - URL: http://127.0.0.1:5002 - Swagger Documentation: http://127.0.0.1:5002/docs

docs.title: 3. Process Documents
docs.text:
You can process documents in several ways:

a. Using the API: 

# Upload a single document
curl -X POST -F "file=@path/to/document.pdf" http://127.0.0.1:5002/api/upload

# Process a document
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"document_id": "123"}' \
     http://127.0.0.1:5002/api/process

b. Using the batch processing script: 

python src/main.py --mode batch_process \
                   --input-dir data/raw \
                   --output-dir data/processed

c. Using the training pipeline: 

# Train the classification model
python src/classification/train_classifier.py \
       --data-dir data/processed \
       --output-dir data/models/classification

# Train the extraction model
python src/extraction/train_extractor.py \
       --data-dir data/processed \
       --output-dir data/models/extraction

tail -f src/invoice_scanner.log

docs.title: Document Quality Challenges
docs.text: Our system is trained to handle various document quality issues:

docs.title: Bad Quality Scenarios
docs.text:
Too Dark Documents

  • Documents with poor contrast

  • Scanned copies with dark backgrounds

  • Faded text on dark paper

  • Solution: Advanced image preprocessing with contrast enhancement

  • Layout Issues

  • Amounts overshadowed by complex layouts

  • Text overlapping with background elements

  • Irregular formatting and positioning

  • Solution: Layout analysis and text isolation algorithms

  • Feeble or Out of Bounds

  • Faint or barely visible text

  • Content extending beyond standard margins

  • Skewed or rotated content

  • Solution: Image enhancement and geometric correction

docs.text:

    "invoice_number": {
        "value": "INV-2024-123",
        "confidence": 0.92,
        "quality_issues": ["slight_fade"],
        "method": "enhanced_ocr"
    },
    "total_amount": {
        "value": "1234.56",
        "confidence": 0.85,
        "quality_issues": ["overshadowed"],
        "method": "layout_analysis"
    }

docs.title: Quality-Based Processing
docs.text:
The system adapts its processing based on document quality:

  1. High Quality Documents (Quality Score > 0.8)
  2. Standard OCR processing
  3. Direct text extraction

  4. Regular confidence thresholds

  5. Medium Quality Documents (Quality Score 0.5-0.8)

  6. Enhanced preprocessing
  7. Multiple OCR passes
  8. Layout analysis

  9. Cross-validation of results

  10. Low Quality Documents (Quality Score < 0.5)

  11. Intensive preprocessing
  12. Advanced enhancement techniques
  13. Multiple extraction methods
  14. Human verification flags

docs.title: Handling Mixed Quality Batches
docs.text:

                   --input-dir data/raw \

This will: - Automatically assess document quality - Apply appropriate preprocessing - Group documents by quality level - Adjust extraction parameters - Generate quality reports
